config.title: Container orchestration

intro.title: Container orchestration
intro.body: In this lesson, you will learn the fundamentals of container orchestration by setting up a simple multi-container application. You will explore core concepts like service discovery, load balancing, and automated deployment using a popular orchestration tool. The main technologies involved include Docker containers and a basic orchestration platform to manage them. By the end, you'll understand how orchestration helps scale and maintain applications efficiently in production environments.
intro.usecase: Container orchestration is the foundational pattern for managing and scaling modern cloud-native applications. It powers the deployment and operation of services in platforms like Kubernetes dashboards, where developers define and monitor pods, services, and deployments. This is critical for ensuring high availability in products like e-commerce sites during traffic surges or for rolling out updates seamlessly in SaaS applications without downtime.

objectives: Configure a basic container orchestration environment
Implement container deployment and scaling commands
Construct a service definition for container networking
Apply health check configurations to containerized applications
Manipulate container resource allocation and limits
Integrate persistent storage with container workloads
Control container lifecycle through orchestration commands

steps.title: Create main container orchestration demonstration component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ContainerOrchestrationDemo that will serve as the main demonstration component. The component should return null for now.
steps.hint: Define a component using either function ContainerOrchestrationDemo() { return null; } or const ContainerOrchestrationDemo = () => { return null; }.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ContainerOrchestrationDemo is created and returns null.
successCriteria: The component is named ContainerOrchestrationDemo and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main container orchestration demonstration component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly ContainerOrchestrationDemo and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you used the correct name and returned null.

steps.title: Initialize state for container cluster data
steps.instruction: Inside your ContainerOrchestrationDemo component, initialize state using useState to hold container cluster information. Create a state variable named 'clusterData' with an initial value of an empty object {}.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook to declare a state variable. The initial state should be an empty object that will later hold cluster data like nodes, pods, and services.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state for data
const [data, setData] = useState({});
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'clusterData' initialized as an empty object, ready to store container orchestration cluster information.
successCriteria: The useState hook is used to create a state variable named 'clusterData' with an initial value of {}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state for container cluster data. The empty object provides a clean structure to later populate with nodes, pods, and services information.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using useState correctly and naming the state variable 'clusterData' with an initial empty object {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on initializing state. You need to use useState to create a state variable named 'clusterData' that starts as an empty object {}.

steps.title: Define handler to scale container replicas
steps.instruction: Inside your ContainerOrchestrationDemo component, create a function named handleScaleReplicas that takes a parameter 'change' and updates the cluster data state accordingly.
steps.hint: Define a function that receives a number (positive to scale up, negative to scale down) and uses the setClusterData function to update the replicas count.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handler function that can modify the number of container replicas, simulating scaling operations in container orchestration.
successCriteria: The component contains a function named handleScaleReplicas that takes a 'change' parameter and updates state using setClusterData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a scaling handler that can increase or decrease container replicas, just like orchestration platforms handle scaling operations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named handleScaleReplicas, takes a 'change' parameter, and properly updates the state using setClusterData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scaling handler isn't quite right. Remember to create a function that can modify the replicas count based on the change parameter.

steps.title: Define handler to redistribute workloads
steps.instruction: Inside your ContainerOrchestrationDemo component, create a handler function named redistributeWorkloads that will handle workload balancing across nodes.
steps.hint: Define a function that will be called to redistribute container workloads. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handler function named redistributeWorkloads is defined inside the component, ready to implement workload redistribution logic.
successCriteria: The redistributeWorkloads function is defined inside the ContainerOrchestrationDemo component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the redistributeWorkloads handler function. This function will handle workload balancing across container nodes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is named exactly 'redistributeWorkloads' and is defined inside the ContainerOrchestrationDemo component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The redistributeWorkloads handler function is not properly defined. Check that you've created a function with the correct name inside the component.

steps.title: Define handler for container health monitoring
steps.instruction: Inside your ContainerOrchestrationDemo component, create a handler function named handleHealthCheck that simulates monitoring container health and performing automatic recovery.
steps.hint: Define a function that logs or updates state to reflect health monitoring actions, such as checking container status and triggering recovery if needed.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handler function named handleHealthCheck is added to the component, ready to simulate health monitoring and recovery logic.
successCriteria: The component includes a function named handleHealthCheck that contains logic for health checks and automatic recovery simulation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a health monitoring handler that can simulate container health checks and recovery actions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a function, but ensure it's named handleHealthCheck and includes logic for health monitoring and recovery simulation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler function for health monitoring is missing or incorrectly defined. Please create a function named handleHealthCheck that simulates health checks and recovery.

steps.title: Create the main orchestration dashboard structure
steps.instruction: In your ContainerOrchestrationDemo component, return a main dashboard container with three sections: one for cluster overview, one for node status, and one for container management.
steps.hint: Create a wrapper element (like a div) with three child elements that will serve as placeholders for each section.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic dashboard structure with three distinct sections for container orchestration monitoring.
successCriteria: The component returns a wrapper element containing three section elements representing cluster overview, node status, and container management areas.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the foundation for your container orchestration dashboard with the three main monitoring sections.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly three section elements inside your main wrapper for cluster overview, node status, and container management.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dashboard structure isn't quite right. You need to return a main wrapper element with three distinct section elements for the different monitoring areas.

steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a <div> element with a heading to display cluster status and metrics.

steps.feedbackPartial: You added some structure, but make sure to include a heading inside the <div>.

steps.title: Add scaling controls and wire to scale handler
steps.instruction: Add a button to increase replicas and a button to decrease replicas inside your dashboard structure, and wire their onClick events to the scale handler function.
steps.hint: Create two button elements with appropriate labels like 'Increase Replicas' and 'Decrease Replicas', then set their onClick props to call your scale handler with the appropriate direction.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two buttons appear in the dashboard UI that allow manual scaling of container replicas when clicked.
successCriteria: The dashboard contains an 'Increase Replicas' button and a 'Decrease Replicas' button, both wired to call the scale handler with appropriate parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added manual scaling controls to your container orchestration dashboard.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some controls, but make sure you have both increase and decrease buttons properly wired to the scale handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scaling controls are missing or not properly connected. Check that you've added two buttons with onClick handlers that call your scale function.

steps.title: Add orchestration automation controls and wire handlers
steps.instruction: Add a section with a button for automated workload balancing and a button for automated health monitoring, wiring each to their respective handlers.
steps.hint: Create two button elements with appropriate labels and onClick handlers that call the redistributeWorkloads and monitorHealth functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboard will include two new buttons for automated orchestration features: one for workload balancing and one for health monitoring.
successCriteria: Two button elements are added with appropriate labels and onClick handlers that call the redistributeWorkloads and monitorHealth functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the automation controls for workload balancing and health monitoring.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some controls, but make sure you have both buttons with proper onClick handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The automation controls are missing or not properly wired. Check that you have two buttons with onClick handlers.
